page: The Vultr vhp-2c-2gb-intel is an entry-tier virtual machine within the High Performance product family, powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled across a shared host allocation. The processor features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting extended instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2. System memory is sized at 2.0 GB (1.0 GB per vCPU), and local storage includes 60 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled, with no hardware GPU acceleration available.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration toward the lower percentile tiers across compute and memory operations. In CPU stress testing, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1384.38 and a multi-core score of 2740.38, reflecting lower-quartile execution capacity. The PassMark CPU test recorded a total score of 3155.94, supported by 2805.34 in extended instructions and 1034.32 in cryptographic testing. Memory throughput benchmarks showed cached small-block reads reaching 197.66 GB/sec, whereas uncached 256 MB reads and writes measured 13.19 GB/sec and 11.09 GB/sec, placing raw uncached throughput in the bottom 10 percent of recorded systems.

Application and network throughput metrics follow similar patterns. Redis SET operations sustained 2.81 million operations per second, while static web serving reached a transfer rate of 2.37 GB/sec. Small 135M-parameter model inference tests registered 133.49 tokens per second for prompt processing and 31.16 tokens per second for generation. The combination of shared Intel vCPUs and a 1:1 memory-to-core ratio delivers cost efficiency for entry-level footprints, though resource contention and 2 GB memory limitations constrain scalability.

The instance is best matched to modest workloads that fit within 2 GB of RAM and benefit from fast local NVMe storage. Suitable scenarios include lightweight web serving, development environments, DNS servers, microservices, small automated scripts, and test instances.

It features 2.0 GB of system memory, 60 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate entry-level execution across standard workloads, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 3155.94, uncached memory read bandwidth of 13.19 GB/sec, and 2.81 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware support includes AVX-512 and AES instructions, though throughput remains bounded by the shared-thread model and constrained memory profile. This server offers cost-effective hardware utilization for lightweight services such as entry-level web hosting, small background workers, utility microservices, and development environments requiring fast local storage.
